citations.A1: `_cache` is a module global filled once and never invalidated ... fix by storing the file's `st_mtime_ns` and `st_size` next to the data and reloading whenever a fresh `os.stat(path)` differs
citations.A2: Not a fix: a time-based TTL still serves stale values for up to the TTL and reloads unchanged files for nothing
citations.A3: Not a fix: deleting the cache and re-reading every call cures staleness but puts a file open and JSON parse on every hot-path call
citations.A4: The `path` argument is ignored after the first call, so a later call with a different file silently returns the first file's data
citations.A5: The check-and-load is not thread-safe, so two threads can both miss the cache and one can read a half-updated tuple; wrap the stat-compare-and-reload in a `threading.Lock`
citations.A6: The cached dict is handed out by reference, so any caller that mutates it changes what everyone sees next
